**`bb.sdk.threads.rateLimitRecovery` exists in the 0.37.x/0.38.x plugin SDK types and is absent from 0.39.0.** Not renamed — removed.

I enumerated every member of `ThreadsArea` in the 0.39.0-generated declarations:

```
archive archiveAll cancelPlan childSummary clearGoal compact conversationOutline
create defaultExecutionOptions delete editMessage environments events fork get
interactions list markRead markUnread open output paneAction pin promptHistory
queuedMessages reorderPinned resolveMentions search send signal spawn stop
storageFiles storagePaths tabs timeline timelineTurnSummaryDetails unarchive
unpin update wait
```

No rate-limit method. `grep -c rateLimitRecovery` returns 1 against the previously committed declarations and **0** against 0.39.0's.

## Impact

A plugin using it stops compiling on upgrade. In our case it backed a usage-cap check that decides whether a role holder is rate-limited before dispatching work to it — so the failure mode if it were stubbed is a silent false negative on exactly the signal that prevents burning a capped seat.

Notably, the previously-built artifact **loaded** cleanly under 0.39.0. That establishes loading, not answering: the call only fires when a cap check runs, so a plugin can appear healthy after upgrade and fail later at the first invocation. Anyone relying on "it loaded, so it's compatible" gets a delayed surprise.
